title: TD expands agentic AI across mortgage operations to make banking faster, simpler and more human
summary: New agentic AI capabilities are designed to double colleague productivity in select mortgage processes, giving teams more time to focus on clients TORONTO, Oct. 13, 2026 /CNW/ -- TD Bank Group...
body_markdown:
New agentic AI capabilities are designed to double colleague productivity in select mortgage processes, giving teams more time to focus on clients


TORONTO


, Oct. 13, 2026


/CNW/ -- TD Bank Group (TD) today announced two new agentic AI capabilities for Real Estate Secured Lending (RESL), expanding the use of AI across the mortgage lifecycle.


In mortgage funding and discharge, the capabilities coordinate multi-step document verification, connect information across systems, and generate outputs for colleague review.


By automating time-intensive tasks, the technology allows colleagues to concentrate on the expertise, judgment and human connection that matter most to clients.


The move builds on TD's May 2026 launch of agentic AI for mortgage pre-adjudication, which reduced average processing time from 15 hours to less than three minutes.


Key takeaways:


- TD is expanding agentic AI across the mortgage lifecycle, from pre-adjudication to parts of mortgage funding and discharge.
- The capabilities coordinate document verification, connect information across systems and flag potential discrepancies.
- Colleagues review AI-generated outputs and remain responsible for decisions requiring human expertise and judgment.


"We're focused on using agentic AI where it can make the biggest difference for our teams and clients," said Mohit Veoli, Senior Vice President, Real Estate Secured Lending at TD. "By simplifying repetitive parts of the mortgage journey, AI can make everyday work easier and reduce friction for clients. Our colleagues remain at the centre, using the technology to augment their expertise and deliver an even better experience."


Taking friction out of mortgage funding and discharge


For mortgage funding, the capability brings essential client and property details into a concise case summary, enabling colleagues to complete the initial review in up to half the time.


For mortgage discharges, the capability assembles the information needed to prepare a discharge statement, with colleagues checking the final output before it is issued.


"AI is becoming an increasingly important part of how we innovate and work," said Maks Volkovs, Senior Vice President and Chief AI Scientist, Layer 6 AI at TD. "Home lending is a powerful example, evolving from a single agentic AI use case to a portfolio of capabilities that work alongside colleagues and give them more time for clients and complex decisions."


Frequently Asked Questions


What is agentic AI?


Agentic AI is a form of artificial intelligence that can coordinate multiple tasks, analyze information across systems, identify relevant insights, generate recommended outputs, and support complex business workflows.


How is TD using agentic AI?


TD uses agentic AI in mortgage pre-adjudication and select mortgage funding and discharge processes, including document review and information validation.


Does agentic AI replace colleagues?


TD's approach is to use AI to augment colleagues, not replace the human expertise and relationships that are central to banking. TD uses a human-in-the-loop approach, meaning AI-generated insights and outputs are reviewed by colleagues, who remain responsible for applying judgment and making decisions.


What are the benefits of Agentic AI for clients?


For clients, agentic AI is designed to support faster, simpler, and more consistent mortgage experiences by reducing administrative friction behind the scenes.


What are the benefits for colleagues?


For colleagues, agentic AI reduces repetitive information gathering and document comparison, connects material from multiple sources and highlights areas requiring attention. This creates more capacity to support clients and manage complex situations.


TD is investing in technology, education, and skills development to help colleagues understand and effectively use AI in their work.


About TD Bank Group


The Toronto-Dominion Bank and its subsidiaries are collectively known as TD Bank Group ("TD" or the "Bank"). TD is the sixth largest bank in North America by assets and serves 28.2 million clients in four key businesses operating in a number of locations in financial centres around the globe: Canadian Personal and Commercial Banking, including TD Canada Trust and TD Auto Finance Canada; U.S. Banking, including TD Auto Finance U.S. and TD Wealth (U.S.); Wealth Management and Insurance, including TD Wealth (Canada), TD Direct Investing and TD Insurance; and Wholesale Banking, including TD Securities and TD Cowen. TD also ranks among North America's leading digital banks, with more than 14 million active mobile users in Canada and the U.S. TD had $2.1 trillion in assets on July 31, 2026. The Toronto-Dominion Bank trades under the symbol "TD" on the Toronto Stock Exchange and New York Stock Exchange.
